info.name: Sentinel
info.summary: Watches the things Nextcloud's own defences do not watch, and tells you when they change
Veghează asupra lucrurilor pe care apărarea proprie a Nextcloud nu le urmărește, și te anunță când se schimbă
info.description:
Nextcloud defends itself well. It throttles password guessing, hashes passwords properly, sets the right headers, offers two-factor authentication, and checks that its own files have not been altered. Sentinel does not repeat any of that.
What it does is answer the questions nobody asks until it is too late. Who has two-factor authentication and who does not. Which public links have no password and no expiry, and have been sitting there for months. Which application passwords were last used in February and are still valid. Whether a file in the installation changed, and whether that change was expected. And when any of it changes, who is told.
* **A posture page** that checks what core does not, with the reason and the fix beside each finding * **A file baseline you can acknowledge**, so a deliberate patch stops raising an alarm and a real change is the only thing that does * **Watchers** that notice an account becoming an administrator, two-factor being switched off, a new application password, or a public link created without a password, and say so * **An inventory** of public links, sessions and application passwords, with the age of each and a way to end them * Every finding explains what it means and what happens if it is ignored, because a warning nobody understands is a warning nobody acts on
Sentinel changes nothing on its own. It reports, and it acts only when asked.
info.author: Cristian Casapu
